rv.q: Mark Strong and Lesley Manville are spellbinding in this wrenchingly tense Greek tragedy

It is not only about a couple doomed by their love but contains cross currents of family drama, from mother-daughter battles to a son’s coming out and profound reflections on life, death and sex. A stop-clock counts the hours and minutes to the election results but also marks the inevitable forward movement to terrible self-knowledge.

The voting has just closed and cameras are following this would-be ruler’s progress to power. To anyone who already knows that Oedipus’s evening will end with him being unable to see anybody or anything, it’s one of a slew of smart ironies in Robert Icke’s riveting modern-day rejig.
Robert Icke’s compassionate political thriller spin on the horrifying Greek tragedy

Sophocles’s incest shocker, Oedipus, has never looked sharper, sicker or more modern. We meet them all at a family meal at campaign HQ with his teenagers and Jocasta, his glamorous wife. Mark Strong, intense and rather scary, is a terrific Oedipus.

Mark Strong’s politician kicks back with his wife (Lesley Manville), his family and his campaign team, confident that his message of change and hope has won the day. But this is Robert Icke’s stunning reworking of Oedipus. As that digital clock in the campaign room counts down remorselessly, we watch in queasy horror.
Any opportunity to see Mark Strong — who takes the title role previously played by Hans Kesting — has to be seized with both hands.
He rashly promises he will do this at the night’s end, despite the concerns of his adviser Creon (Michael Gould).

But Oedipus isn’t immune to the old ways, either, something that Icke shows by patterning riddles and wordplay through his text, inescapable as political spin. “We live under blankets feathered with lies,” says Jocasta, as deceptions pile up. The couple’s three children arrive for an election night dinner bringing awkward truths.
The adaptation excels in the way that Icke identifies the tragedy as being not of one man
Strong and Manville share great chemistry
